CVE-2021-3711.title: SM2 Decryption Buffer Overflow
CVE-2021-3711.description: In order to decrypt SM2 encrypted data an application is expected to call the API function EVP_PKEY_decrypt(). Typically an application will call this function twice. The first time, on entry, the "out" parameter can be NULL and, on exit, the "outlen" parameter is populated with the buffer size required to hold the decrypted plaintext. The application can then allocate a sufficiently sized buffer and call EVP_PKEY_decrypt() again, but this time passing a non-NULL value for the "out" parameter. A bug in the implementation of the SM2 decryption code means that the calculation of the buffer size required to hold the plaintext returned by the first call to EVP_PKEY_decrypt() can be smaller than the actual size required by the second call. This can lead to a buffer overflow when EVP_PKEY_decrypt() is called by the application a second time with a buffer that is too small. CsvEncoder::decode() splits each header cell on the key separator, . by default, and nests the decoded rows one level per separator, with no limit. PHP frees nested arrays recursively, so freeing data that is nested deeply enough overflows the C stack and crashes the process. With a stack of 8 MB, a CSV body of 448 KB is enough.

Each row also builds all the levels of its headers again. With a deep header, a CSV body of 2 KB made of short rows allocates more than 128 MB. A body of 1 MB keeps the CPU busy for 10 seconds or more.

CVE-2026-135244.title: MISP: Client IP Spoofing via Unvalidated Forwarded Header Bypasses IP Restrictions and Brute-Force Protection
CVE-2026-135244.description:
MISP trusted client-supplied forwarded IP headers (such as X-Forwarded-For) without verifying that the request originated from a known proxy or that the value was a valid IP address. The configured header value was accepted as the authoritative client IP for all security-relevant functions.

An unauthenticated remote attacker could forge the forwarded header to:
- Bypass IP-based restrictions on API authentication keys
- Evade brute-force / rate-limiting protection
- Inject arbitrary values into application and ECS logs, corrupting audit trails

The vulnerability required the MISP.log_client_ip_header setting to be configured to a forwarded header (e.g. HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR), which is a common deployment when MISP sits behind a reverse proxy.

Affected: MISP versions prior to 2.5.52

CVE-2026-99632.title: drm/amdkfd: use the queue's process info for the WPTR BO eviction fence
CVE-2026-99632.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/amdkfd: use the queue's process info for the WPTR BO eviction fence

amdgpu_amdkfd_map_gtt_bo_to_gart() removes the eviction fence of
bo->vm_bo->vm->process_info from the WPTR BO of a new queue. bo->vm_bo
is the VM which opened the BO last, not necessarily the KFD process' VM,
and a render node VM has no process info.

On navi31, an unprivileged process which exports its WPTR BO with
AMDKFD_IOC_EXPORT_DMABUF and imports it on a second render node fd
oopses in AMDKFD_IOC_CREATE_QUEUE:

BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000060
RIP: 0010:amdgpu_amdkfd_map_gtt_bo_to_gart+0x86/0x1a0 [amdgpu]
init_user_queue.part.0+0x180/0x250 [amdgpu]
pqm_create_queue+0x32d/0x730 [amdgpu]
kfd_ioctl_create_queue+0x583/0x9f0 [amdgpu]

Pass the process info of the queue instead. With the fix, the queue is
created and destroyed normally.
